programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Some bonds can't be broken-like a mother's love or a killer's grip on his victim. Al, Kellie, and her daughter Hailey move into a Montreal townhouse, aware of its tragic past. A teen girl, evicted with her mother, took her own life. But death wasn't the end. Haunting audio recordings reveal she has returned-with a follower. As Al obsesses over a past murder, Kellie fears a killer still lurks.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Children often feel powerless in the face of the adult world. In Glen Burnie, Maryland, 10-year-old Billy Bean's life is already in crisis. He and his sister are attacked at night-pinned to their beds by unseen forces. Billy senses an evil presence destroying his family. As the attacks worsen, he fights to uncover the dark secrets of the house on Little Road before he loses everything.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Evil thrives on deception, slowly eroding faith and family bonds. Sarah Miller senses something supernatural in her home, terrifying her children and making her question reality. Her boyfriend's skepticism deepens the divide as a demonic force tightens its grip. A religious demonologist identifies a diabolical infestation and prepares a ritual to expel the entity before it destroys them.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: In life, people can be tormented by their own crimes. The same may be true in death. In Wilder, Kentucky, a nightclub stands by the Licking River, said to draw murderers and Satanists. Club owner Bobby Mackey dismisses the legends-until his wife and an employee are attacked by unseen forces. Beneath the club, an old slaughterhouse well harbors an ancient evil, waiting to claim its next victims.

programme.title: Ark of The Covenant: New Evidence?
programme.desc: It is a quest that has fascinated scholars and adventurers for century after century. What happened to that treasure and centerpiece of ancient Jewish life - the Ark of the Covenant? No one knows what happened to it, but researchers never give up seeking for this which will no doubt rank among history's greatest finds if it is ever discovered.

programme.title: The Night of the Long Knives: Hitler's Rise to Power
programme.desc: The Night of the Long Knives is considered the first act of horror committed by the Nazis. What happened in Germany, and in Hitler's rise to power, that led to this purge in 1934? Caught between the conservative tendency and the revolutionary aspirations that were dividing the country, the Chancellor had a choice. To calm the rumors of a military coup against him, Hitler sent a clear message.

programme.title: The Egyptians
programme.desc: From architecture to necropolises or shipbuilding discover the Egyptian symbols that have survived through the ages and what they mean today.

programme.title: The Viking Myths
programme.desc: Meanwhile, Kvasir (the being born out of peace) goes out into the world and answers all questions with ease. So much so that the two dwarf brothers capture Kvasir, murder him, drain his blood and mix it with mead: thus creating the Mead of Poetry, a metaphor for poetic inspiration.

programme.title: The Viking Myths
programme.desc: Asgard, the kingdom of the Aesir, is under threat from monstrous creatures. To save Asgard, Odin embarks on an initiatory journey, during which he faces terrible trials to acquire knowledge: he loses his eye before being hanged for nine nights without eating or drinking, his side pierced by a spear.

programme.title: The Ace's War
programme.desc: Winter 1914. The first world conflict is becoming bogged down in the trenches. From now on, the war will no longer be solely on the ground. It will also be in the air. But the beginnings are difficult.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths: The Iliad
programme.desc: Agamemnon has seen it in a dream: Troy will be taken today. Helen's husband Menelaus recognizes Paris, the man who took his wife. The two men decide to face each other in a duel.

programme.title: The Destiny of Rome
programme.desc: The Battle of Philippi in 42 BC would change the world forever. Marc Antony and Octavian sought to avenge Caesar, but later fought over his legacy, with the fate of Rome in the balance. They first managed to combine their forces to punish Brutus and Cassius, Caesar's assassins, and to proclaim their legitimacy. But there could only be one successor to Caesar.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths
programme.desc: On his quest to find the Golden Fleece, Jason asked the cruel King of Colchis and his daughter Medea, a powerful sorceress, for help. Medea fell in love with Jason, helped him to find the precious Fleece, and fled with him.

programme.title: Henry VIII: The Tyrant King and His Six Wives
programme.desc: In the initial episode Tracy Borman shows us exclusive access to parts of Henry VII's life. From his wedding bed to the Tudor Bedding Ceremony and the realities of childbirth. We learn more about the Tudor's philosophy on sex and extramarital affairs as it pertains to Henry VII.

programme.title: Her Majesty The Queen Mother: 1900-2002
programme.desc: When Her Majesty the Queen Mother died peacefully in her sleep aged 101, the nation lost one of its best-loved royals. Throughout her extraordinary life spanning the whole of the 20th century, the Queen Mother had a remarkable ability to reach ordinary people. Her life was one of duty, serving the nation.

programme.title: Castles & Palaces of Europe
programme.desc: On the Isle of Wight, the baroque ruins of Appuldurcrombe House, bombed during World War 2, are famous for their ghosts. Over on the mainland, Blenheim Palace has gone down in history for more orthodox reasons: a gift from Queen Anne to the Duke of Marlborough in the 18th century, this building, which is imbued with history, is the birthplace of Sir Winston Churchill.

programme.title: Caligula's Hidden Legacy
programme.desc: New discoveries beneath the Vatican reveal the grand designs of Caligula. Beyond the legend of a mad tyrant emerges a ruler driven by ambition-building colossal aqueducts, transporting the Vatican obelisk from Egypt, and staging feats of engineering that defied nature. This episode reconsiders Caligula as a visionary determined to reshape Rome in his own image.

programme.title: Impossible Peace
programme.desc: After four years of fighting, World War I ends. The victorious nations assemble at Versailles to design the peace that they will impose on the defeated - Germany and Austria-Hungary. Russia's Bolshevik revolution has become a murderous civil war. The map of Europe is remade, with the dismantling and collapse of old empires.

programme.title: The Viking Myths
programme.desc: A banquet is held in Asgard, during which Loki insults the gods, revealing their weaknesses. His punishment is terrible. Chained under venom that periodically drips on him, he must watch as two of his sons are killed, one of them devouring the other. Odin knows that Ragnarök is not far off, since Loki is now, according to the seer's prediction, in chains. And when he breaks free of his chains...

programme.title: The Egyptians
programme.desc: Archaeologist Zahi Hawass has been excavating the ancient necropolis of Saqqara, south of Cairo, for several decades. Today, he hopes to discover the tomb of Imhotep, the architect of the first pyramid in the history of mankind: the Step Pyramid of Djoser. With his team, Hawass will unearth marvellous tombs, and the many secrets of the Egyptian mummies they contain...

programme.title: Life in the Time of
programme.desc: In the 17th century, a young man from Gascony wanted to join the prestigious regiments of musketeers of the King of France. To this end, he trains daily in an academy of gentlemen in the handling of weapons and equestrian art. He thus hopes to be noticed by an officer. But the selection is ruthless: you have to be the best to join the Musketeers.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths: The Odyssey
programme.desc: Odysseus has been living out peaceful days with Calypso for 7 years. But waves of nostalgia wash over him, and the memories of his wife, his son and his island never cease to torment him. Hermes, sent by Zeus, under pressure from Athena, comes to ask Calypso to let the king of Ithaca leave.

programme.title: The Last Mystery of Cleopatra
programme.desc: Even from her grave, Egyptian Queen Cleopatra continues to mystify scholars and common people alike! The debate about the way she looked, her mysterious death & her lost tomb continues today even as more evidence of her glorious reign comes to the surface. Whether she died from a snake bite or not, the whereabouts of her mummy - unanswered questions lead scholars on quest about the enigmatic royal.

programme.title: Secrets in the Bones: The Hunt for the Black Death Killer
programme.desc: It was called the Black Death, a disease that started in the 14th century, and swept across Europe wiping out half the population, one of the most lethal killers in human history. But the cause of the Black Death has eluded scientists. Now, Evolutionary biologist Hendrik Poinar embarks on an epic journey to solve the 600-year old mystery and change the way we fight infectious diseases today.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Modern science suggests we are all connected by energy. This may explain why Romie feels drawn to an abandoned house in Tucson, Arizona. After moving in, nightmares bleed into reality, and she sees a shadowy spirit. A clairvoyant urges her to communicate with it, but fear holds her back. As the entity targets only her, Romie begins to question her sanity-is the house haunted, or is she cursed?

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Some believe knowledge comes from reason, others from intuition. When Selena moves into an old Michigan house, she senses danger. The attic makes her dizzy, the kitchen feels watched, and photos reveal ghostly faces. With proof of a haunting, she and her sister seek a psychic's help. He confirms the worst-the house is a place of suffering, trapping both the living and the dead.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: The Fahey family has lived in their Galway townhouse for decades. When Martha brings home her newborn, eerie disturbances begin. Unexplained cries echo through the night, objects vanish, and a chilling presence fills the house. A priest offers no relief, but a healer reveals a dark secret-Martha's child has awakened the psychic energy of a long-buried crime that prayer alone cannot erase.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Some believe knowledge comes from reason, others from intuition. When Selena moves into an old Michigan house, she senses danger. The attic makes her dizzy, the kitchen feels watched, and photos reveal ghostly faces. With proof of a haunting, she and her sister seek a psychic's help. He confirms the worst-the house is a place of suffering, trapping both the living and the dead.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Time slowly erases reminders of the past. Old roads are abandoned, and their destinations forgotten. When Clara's family moves to rural Hinsdale, NY, they expect peace but find eerie disturbances. Ritualistic chanting echoes from the woods, and neighbors whisper of roaming ghosts. A psychic warns that spirits are drawn to their home-and to a gruesome secret hidden in the crawlspace.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: In this world, evil lurks in both shadows and unassuming places. It deceives and destroys. When Bonnie's family buys a 19th-century Connecticut farmhouse, they feel watched. After unseen entities attack her children, they seek out psychic investigators. As events grow violent, Bonnie forms a psychic link to the past, and investigators witness the haunting escalate from obsession to possession.

programme.title: Besieged Fortresses - Legendary Battles
programme.desc: Constantinople, the jewel of the Byzantine Empire, has stood for a thousand years. Now, Sultan Mehmed II leads an army, and a stunning new superweapon, against this last remnant of Christianity in the East. But Emperor Constantin XI knows his fortress and will fight to the death to keep it.

programme.title: Besieged Fortresses - Legendary Battles
programme.desc: When Saladin invades Jerusalem, Philip Augustus and Richard the Lionheart put their rivalry aside to fight for Saint-John of Acre, a highly strategic port in the Holy land. At the head of 25,000 men, the former enemies take on the Sultan in the first battle of the Third Crusade.

programme.title: The Destiny of Rome
programme.desc: Ten years later, the supreme strategist Octavian waged the naval battle of Actium against his former ally, who now had the backing of Cleopatra. Octavian put an end to Antony and Cleopatra's military ambitions and became the first Roman emperor under the name of Augustus. Witness the last moments of the Roman Republic, marked by this terrible duel between two men hungry for glory.

programme.title: Revolt! The American Revolution 1775 - 1783
programme.desc: How is it that thirteen small colonies in North America were able to succeed - against a global power such as Great Britain? Learn about the seven-year war, the Boston Tea Party and the origin of the Declaration of Independence. Once the War of Independence was won, why did it take years to write the Constitution? And what was life like afterwards, and how did Native Americans and slaves fare?

programme.title: Ark of the Covenant Revealed
programme.desc: According to the Bible, The Ark of the Covenant was a box which housed the two tablets of stone inscribed with the Ten Commandments. It was constructed by a man called Belazeel on Mount Sinai in Ancient Egypt to the instructions given to Moses by God. This film aims to shed new light on the Ark of the Covenant and perhaps finally unravel the truth behind one of the greatest biblical mysteries.

programme.title: The Last Seven Months of Anne Frank
programme.desc: Anne Frank's surviving friends tell the story that begins where her famous diary leaves off and for the first time the concentration camp experiences of Anne and her family are told. Amongt the eyewitnesses is Anne Frank's closest friend, identified as 'Lies' in Anne's diary. She was filmed at several locations where she had been with Anne, including Bergen-Belsen concentration camp.

programme.title: Operation Valkyrie: The Plot to Assassinate Hitler
programme.desc: On July 20th, 1944 a group of German conspirators lead by Claus von Stauffenberg attempted to assassinate Adolf Hitler himself. The plan was to remove the Nazi Party from power, and then make peace with the Allied Forces to end the bloodshed and show the world that not all Germans were like Hitler. However, the plot failed and lead to nearly 5,000 executions.

programme.title: The Egyptians
programme.desc: Despite months of excavation yielding numerous sarcophagi, Zahi Hawass discovers a stone coffin hinting at a vizier's presence from the New Kingdom. Yet, inside, an unexpected surprise awaits. The revelation of a mysterious queen, previously found, reignites investigations, challenging established Egyptological beliefs. Will these latest findings reshape our understanding of ancient history?

programme.title: The Viking Myths
programme.desc: After a protracted war, the Vanes and Aesir seal the peace with an exchange of hostages. Mímir, Odin's faithful advisor, also goes to live with the Vanes. Asgard must be rebuilt: the wall has been destroyed. A master builder arrives and offers to rebuild it in three seasons. In return, he demands the moon and the sun.

programme.title: Revolt! The Russian Revolution March 1917 - November 1917
programme.desc: The Russian Revolution, actually two rebellions, was a revolution that destroyed the Tsarist autocracy, and helped create the Soviet Union. Learn about Lenin, the Bolsheviks, communism, the notorious Rasputin, rumors of cannibalism, and acute poverty. All of which led to a revolution, a coup d'état and a civil war.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths
programme.desc: Zeus had a reputation for being a seducer of women. One day he lay with a mortal - Semele, the daughter of the king of Thebes. Their son Dionysos was brought up by nymphs. One day he discovered the vine, and decided to travel the world teaching mankind the art of making wine out of it.

programme.title: The Real Joan of Arc
programme.desc: The myth of Joan of Arc has fascinated people the world over. In the collective memory, she is the young shepherd girl who died at the stake having saved France. But 15th century chronicles report that following events in Rouen, certain people refused to believe she was dead and that another woman was burned instead.

programme.title: Europe - History Seen From Above
programme.desc: Before Spain was Spain, it was Hispania. Roman troops landed in Ampurias in 218 BC, bringing centuries of stability that reshaped the Iberian Peninsula. Roads, aqueducts, bridges, and great cities transformed the landscape, many still visible today. Hispania became a jewel of Rome, a vital economic hub, and a bastion of empire that produced influential leaders and governors.

programme.title: Hidden Side of World War II
programme.desc: This episode explores the second turning point that led to the end of the war - the liberation of France.

programme.title: The Romanovs
programme.desc: Although he had tremendous foresight in his attempts to modernize Russia and enact effective foreign policies, Peter neglected to name an heir before his death in 1725.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths
programme.desc: Bellerophon, the grandson of Sisyphus, one of the Greek world's worst criminals, dreamt of becoming a hero, of being equal to the Gods. But his plans got off to a bad start with the accidental murder of his brother. Forced into exile, he took refuge in Tyrins.

programme.title: The Egyptians
programme.desc: Two hundred years ago, Jean-François Champollion deciphered the Egyptian hieroglyphs for the first time, thus solving one of the greatest enigmas in the history of humanity.

programme.title: The Last Journey of the Vikings
programme.desc: The Vikings have turned from a monastic robbery into a power struggle for the crown. The battle of Hastings 1066 marks the end of the Viking Age, but with the victorious Vilhjálmur a new era begins.

programme.title: The Last Journey of the Vikings
programme.desc: In the French Empire, the Vikings come face to face with new defenses and Charlemagne refuses to hand over Christian land to pagans and pirates. The defense continues but then changes.

programme.title: Napoleon Bonaparte: The Egyptian Campaign
programme.desc: The Directoire had ordered Napoleon Bonaparte to threaten English assets in the Indies by planning a lasting occupation of Egypt. But the country had many surprises in store for all on the mission. We follow this military expedition through the eyes of two young scientists, Villiers and Jollois, who spent three long years enthusiastically trying to spread the ideas of the Enlightenment.

programme.title: Napoleon Bonaparte: The Egyptian Campaign
programme.desc: Exploring Egypt proved more challenging than anticipated. Between the cultural shock, divergence of interests between the military and scientific communities, the epic combat with Mamelukes and Ottomans, popular uprisings, and outbreaks of the plague, this was an expedition to remember.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Children often feel powerless in the face of the adult world. In Glen Burnie, Maryland, 10-year-old Billy Bean's life is already in crisis. He and his sister are attacked at night-pinned to their beds by unseen forces. Billy senses an evil presence destroying his family. As the attacks worsen, he fights to uncover the dark secrets of the house on Little Road before he loses everything.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: The Bible tells of a man possessed by a legion of demons. In Stamford, Connecticut, 12-year-old David has nightmares of a demonic old man flying toward his home. His terror grows daily. His mother is unsure how to respond-until David is physically attacked by an unseen force. Paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren discover demons within him. They must act before he is lost to darkness.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: In Taiwan, many believe the spiritual and material worlds are intertwined. When an American family moves into a lavish mansion in the Yangmingshan Mountains, they witness disturbing supernatural events. Skeptical at first, they refuse to believe in ghosts-until their youngest daughter becomes possessed. A Taoist priest reveals the house was designed to empower the dead and torment the living.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Ron and Nancy believe their historic Baltimore home is perfect. But the seller warns, 'I hope you're good fighters.' At first, they battle faulty wiring and strange plumbing issues. Then, objects move on their own, and Nancy dreams of an old woman laughing as their house burns. As the haunting increases, they realize their home is a gateway between life and death-and someone tried to seal it shut.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: April and Matt buy a Victorian home in Salt Lake City, eager to restore it. But an unseen force detests change. Renovations stall, voices whisper, and April's son sees movement in his closet. Then, a dark entity appears, determined to drive them out. A medium warns that the house holds tormented children's spirits-and if they don't fight back, they too will become forgotten.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: It's said that every photograph steals a piece of a soul. What happens when the subject is dead? Lisa becomes obsessed with a photo of her boyfriend's brother, killed in Vietnam. As her fixation deepens, she experiences waking visions of the soldier and believes the picture has a life of its own. When her daughters report supernatural encounters, Lisa realizes the spirit is taking control.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths
programme.desc: In this myth, many versions of which have been passed down through the ages, Psyche is the Beauty. Concerned that his daughter did not have a suitor, Psyche's father consulted Pythia, who announced grave news: Psyche's father must leave her on a hilltop, from where a monster would come take her away.

programme.title: Endangered Civilizations
programme.desc: This boy riding a poney is called Josh Guerrero : he is 8 years old. He is a Lakota. 100 years after the 'Massacre of Wounded Knee', the Sioux Lakota decided to commemorate the death of Big Foot. In spite of dreadful weather conditions, Josh decides to follow up this march, as if it were his own initiatic journey to become an Indian warior.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths: The Odyssey
programme.desc: The Suitors, informed by Melantho - one of Penelope's servants - learned that the queen had fooled them. They locked her up in the gynaeceum. Meanwhile, Odysseus meets Athena who tells him that he is indeed in Ithaca.

programme.title: Elizabeth I
programme.desc: Amy Robsart was the wife of Robert Dudley, one of England's leading noblemen. He was believed to be the lover of Queen Elizabeth I. Rumours had circulated that the Queen wanted Amy dead. So when Amy was found at the bottom of a staircase in her Oxfordshire home, few believed it to be an accident, and many openly talked of how the Queen and Dudley had conspired to murder Amy.

programme.title: Imperium - Vespasian: The Path to Power
programme.desc: Vespasian, one of the Roman Empire's finest emperors remains largely unknown. Yet his reign in 1st century AD transitioned a weakening Empire into a period of stability and growth that was the legacy of the other great emperors Trajan, Hadrian, Marcus Aurelius and Septimius Severus. Vespasian ultimately saved Rome from disaster and made possible the Golden Age of the 2nd century AD.

programme.title: Europe - History Seen From Above
programme.desc: From 1936 to 1939, Spain's Civil War killed over 600,000 and left scars Franco's dictatorship could not erase. Seen from above are haunting reminders: Belchite's ruins, Guernica, Francoist monuments, mass graves, and the Valle de los Caídos. Even the concrete sprawl of the Costa del Sol reflects the silence and repression that shaped Spain for nearly 40 years under authoritarian rule.

programme.title: The Viking Myths
programme.desc: To appease Thor's fury, Loki, who has gone to the kingdom of the Dwarves, orders three wondrous objects - among which Thor's hammer, Mjölnir.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths
programme.desc: Kronos revolted against his father Uranus. He severed his father's genitals, and threw them into the sea, where they mingled with the foam and gave birth to Aphrodite. Aphrodite was born from this highly unusual union. She inspired romantic love and physical attraction in equal measure.

programme.title: Europe - History Seen From Above
programme.desc: Spain's landscapes of castles and ramparts reveal a territory divided for centuries. From the Arab invasions of the 8th century, Christian kingdoms launched the Reconquista, a crusade lasting nearly 800 years. Mobilizing warriors across Europe, it left indelible marks-fortresses, walled towns, and battlegrounds-culminating in 1492 with Granada's fall, uniting Spain under Christian rule.

programme.title: Europe - History Seen From Above
programme.desc: From the air, Britain's rural landscape seems wild-fields, heathlands, forests. In truth, it was shaped by centuries of reclamation, deforestation, and farming. Later, aristocrats drew inspiration from nature to create the famed English garden, distinct from continental designs.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths: The Iliad
programme.desc: The River Scamander and its banks are set alight by fireballs sent by the god Hephaestus. The river god spares Achilles, who immediately goes back on the rampage. The gods are shocked by his rage.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths
programme.desc: Dedalus, a prominent Greek inventor, settled in Crete among King Minos' court. Queen Pasiphaë, who had an all-consuming passion for a white bull, called upon his services. Dedalus found a way to allow Pasiphaë to mate with the bull, and Minos locked Daedalus and his son, Icarus, away for their betrayal. Dedalus found a way to escape - but his method put his own son's life in peril.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths: The Iliad
programme.desc: All of the Greek kings and their armies have responded to Agamemnon's call... All except two, that is: Odysseus, and Achilles.

programme.title: Gehlen: Hitler's Superspy
programme.desc: Reinhard Gehlen was Hitler's Chief of Intelligence on the Russian Front during WWII. Before May 1945 he had secreted himself and the files on the Soviets away from Berlin. He then bargained for his freedom with the advancing Americans and his files formed the basis of the CIA when it was set up in 1947. The story traces Gehlen's joining the Nazi party to his retirement on a CIA pension.

programme.title: Life in the Time of
programme.desc: Cro-Magnon man lived 20,000 years ago. One of them, Tashar, is a teenage boy who leads a peaceful life in a clan led by Chaleg. One day, he meets Yaline, a young woman from another clan subject to a barter concluded by Chaleg. Telling the story of this prehistoric adolescent allows you to immerse yourself in these fierce ages and discover the daily life of Cro-Magnon men.

programme.title: The Man Who Cracked the Nazi Code
programme.desc: 6 June 1944. D-Day. The biggest land and sea operation in history. On this pivotal moment in history when the outcome of the Second World War was at stake, much has been recounted, analyzed and examined and yet, the D-Day landings were only possible thanks to a socially-awkward, antimilitarist mathematician named Alan Turing and his field was the most fundamental branch of mathematics: logic.

programme.title: Megapolis: The Ancient World Revealed
programme.desc: Embark on a journey to ancient Rome with stunning computer-generated reconstructions. Witness the secrets of Roman architecture and the ingenuity of its builders. Through recent film footage and post-production magic, iconic monuments like the Pantheon, Nero's palace, and the Coliseum are resurrected, showcasing Rome's excellence, innovation, and eternal beauty.

programme.title: Inside The Tower of London: Crimes, Conspiracies, Confessions
programme.desc: Alice Tankerville and her attempts to 'woo' her way out of trouble with a prison guard; how Watt Tyler led the only force to storm the Tower; and how the legend grew that if you took the Tower you took the country.

programme.title: Alexander the Great: The Macedonian
programme.desc: A close look at Alexander the Great - from Macedonia to India. Alexander the Great has always enjoyed a unique status in history. To the Greeks and Romans, he was a hero, to the Arabs, he was a prophet, to Westerners, he is a myth.

programme.title: Ships That Changed the World
programme.desc: Gigantic sea-faring vessels were the pride and joy of late 19th century Europe. An Irish-German alliance of entrepreneurs saw the founding of ship-builders Harland and Wolff in Belfast, fueling the city's industry. Despite disasters such as the Titanic, ship designs became increasingly utilitarian as inter-European tensions increased, epitomized by the arrival of the Dreadnaught in 1906.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths: The Iliad
programme.desc: Ten years have passed since the Greek forces arrived in Troy, but King Priam's city has still not fallen. The king's eldest son, Hector, reproaches his brother Paris for causing this war with no end.

programme.title: The Napoleonic Wars - The War of the Sixth Coalition
programme.desc: Crossing into France, the Russian army marches steadily toward Napoleon's heartland. In 1814, Russian bayonets pierce the defenses of Paris. With the French capital captured, Europe is finally freed from Napoleon's iron grip-and a new era begins.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths
programme.desc: To earn the title of Master of Olympus, Zeus took many important steps, and overcame many challenges. His story is one of an incredible conquest of power, dating back to time immemorial, when the world began. Born from Chaos, Gaia - Mother Earth - mated with Uranus, the sky.

programme.title: The Napoleonic Wars - The War of the Sixth Coalition
programme.desc: The Battle of Leipzig becomes the largest and bloodiest battle in Europe prior to World War I. Known as the 'Battle of Nations,' it breaks the backbone of Napoleon's army. With France in retreat, Russian troops prepare to take the fight into enemy territory.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Childhood fear is pure, untempered by adult rationality. After his divorce, Steven LaChance dismisses his children's nightmares as stress-until he experiences chilling disturbances himself. Shadows lurk, screams echo, and an unseen force preys on them. He flees, but when another family moves in, he vows to help them. If you enter the spirit world, the spirits enter yours.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: In this world, evil lurks in both shadows and unassuming places. It deceives and destroys. When Bonnie's family buys a 19th-century Connecticut farmhouse, they feel watched. After unseen entities attack her children, they seek out psychic investigators. As events grow violent, Bonnie forms a psychic link to the past, and investigators witness the haunting escalate from obsession to possession.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Some bonds can't be broken-like a mother's love or a killer's grip on his victim. Al, Kellie, and her daughter Hailey move into a Montreal townhouse, aware of its tragic past. A teen girl, evicted with her mother, took her own life. But death wasn't the end. Haunting audio recordings reveal she has returned-with a follower. As Al obsesses over a past murder, Kellie fears a killer still lurks.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Some believe ghosts are human spirits seeking peace, while others say they are inhuman entities that feed on fear. Jan's lonely son Cody seems happy with his imaginary friend-until his behavior turns violent. When Cody reveals his friend lives in a red box in a cemetery, Jan seeks help from a Native American shaman. Through ancient rituals, she battles a force far more sinister than a lost soul.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: In Taiwan, many believe the spiritual and material worlds are intertwined. When an American family moves into a lavish mansion in the Yangmingshan Mountains, they witness disturbing supernatural events. Skeptical at first, they refuse to believe in ghosts-until their youngest daughter becomes possessed. A Taoist priest reveals the house was designed to empower the dead and torment the living.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Modern science suggests we are all connected by energy. This may explain why Romie feels drawn to an abandoned house in Tucson, Arizona. After moving in, nightmares bleed into reality, and she sees a shadowy spirit. A clairvoyant urges her to communicate with it, but fear holds her back. As the entity targets only her, Romie begins to question her sanity-is the house haunted, or is she cursed?

programme.title: The Mysteries of the Bayeux Tapestry
programme.desc: The Bayeux Tapestry, a 70-meter masterpiece from the 11th century, recounts William the Conqueror's capture of England. Despite its fame, no record from its time mentions it, leaving mysteries about its origins and purpose. With 623 figures, animals, and vivid scenes, it is both artwork and historical witness, marking the end of Viking invasions and the dawn of the feudal age of knights.

programme.title: The History of Tanks
programme.desc: Documenting the changing face of tank warfare over the past 100 years, this fascinating documentary is not to be missed by those with an interest in military history and weapon development.

programme.title: The Rise and Fall of Versailles
programme.desc: French people are starving, but the aristocracy is too busy partying inside the palace of Versailles to take notice. Louis tries to make a difference, but every attempt at reform is blocked by his greedy relatives. As he drifts into depression and madness, Louis and his Queen attempt to stave off a revolution, pleading with the nobility to accept reform. But it is too late.

programme.title: Queen Victoria & Kaiser Wilhem II
programme.desc: Queen Victoria's eldest child, Vicky, married the German Crown Prince in 1858. Vicky later endured a difficult birth that almost ended her life and left her baby, the future Kaiser Wilhelm II, with a permanently paralysed arm. Soon Vicky presided over a series of bizarre and cruel attempts to cure Wilhelm of his disability. These procedures created a highly dysfunctional relationship between them.

programme.title: The Vietnam War: Unknown Images
programme.desc: From snake-infested jungles to treacherous underground tunnel complexes to city streets, U.S. Infantrymen had to fight in all terrains in Vietnam. Superb combat footage records the war as it raged both in the countryside and in the cities of Saigon and Hue during the Tet Offensive of 1968.

programme.title: Luther vs. Rome
programme.desc: When Martin Luther nailed his 95 'points for discussion' to Wittenberg's Castle church, his life exploded into an international confrontation, an argument with the Pope and the Protestant Reformation. A monk pitted against the might of Rome. But while the religious, social, and political consequences have been much discussed, we reveal a fundamentally human story of honesty, faith, and fortitude.

programme.title: Europe - History Seen From Above
programme.desc: In 711, Arab and Berber troops crossed Gibraltar, defeating the Visigoths at Guadalete and spreading rapidly across Iberia. Within five years, Al-Andalus stretched from south to Galicia. For nearly eight centuries, Muslim rule left a lasting mark-enriching Spanish culture, transforming cities, and building mosques, palaces, and landmarks that remain central to Spain's heritage today.

programme.title: Inside The Tower of London: Crimes, Conspiracies, Confessions
programme.desc: Bishop Bonner, who tortured both Catholics and Protestants in the turbulent years following the reign of Henry VIII; why the Tower was constructed, why it was built, where it is, how it developed and how the first prisoner it held remains the only on etc escape from the White Tower. We also hear about Lady Jane Grey, and speak to a Beefeater about their role and unique traditions.

programme.title: Mysteries of Noah and The Flood
programme.desc: The Biblical tale of Noah and the Flood holds an unmatched fascination for people of all ages and cultures. The search for irrefutable evidence of a flood so overwhelming that it divided known history into BEFORE and AFTER...and the search for the Ark itself...have long consumed scientists, explorers, religious scholars and artists.

programme.title: William the Conqueror
programme.desc: Normandy, France, the 11th century. Guillaume 'Le Bâtard', known in English as William the Conqueror, succeeded his father as Duke of Normandy at the age of eight. Despite being impetuous, he was a shrewd strategist who turned Normandy into a powerful duchy, feared by the king of France.

programme.title: The Egyptians
programme.desc: Built for pharaoh Khufu over 4,500 years ago, the Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the Seven Wonders still standing today - and is by far the most famous of all pyramids! Yet, this jewel still holds many secrets. Thanks to an exceptional behind-the-scenes access, we'll try to unravel remaining mysteries. Secret chambers have much to reveal about the origins of this stone giant!

programme.title: Ancient Megacities
programme.desc: Persepolis, once envisioned as the Middle East's Garden of Eden, epitomizes opulence and empire. Through centuries and archaeological finds, its mysteries unravel. Explore how this marvel emerged, its true role unveiled by recent discoveries. Witness the tragic destruction of centuries of architectural brilliance in mere hours. Persepolis unveils its astounding secrets in this captivating journey.

programme.title: Hidden Side of World War II
programme.desc: This section takes a look behind the scenes at D-Day, revealing confidential decisions taken by the rulers, as well as the involvement of top-ranking officers and secret agents in the operations.

programme.title: Europe - History Seen From Above
programme.desc: In the 19th century, coal powered Britain's rise as the world's industrial leader. Mining reshaped South Wales, fueling railways, factories, and cities like Manchester and Birmingham. Workers flocked to urban neighborhoods of back-to-back houses, forging a new social fabric. This transformation, both economic and physical, marked an era when landscapes and lives were remade at unprecedented speed.

programme.title: 1000 AD: Anglo-Saxons vs Vikings
programme.desc: What was it really like to live just before the end of the first millennium? 1000 AD recreates life circa 999 AD, showing the everyday lives, loves and passions of the Anglo-Saxon people. A soap opera-style drama runs alongside interviews with leading historians who paint a revealing picture of the political and social structure of pre-Norman Britain.

programme.title: Castles & Palaces of Europe
programme.desc: The former hunting lodge of Beauregard houses an astonishing portrait gallery. Straddling the river Cher, Chenonceau is also known as the 'Castle of Ladies', in reference to its successive female residents - Diane de Poitiers and Catherine de Médicis. The Garden of Love and Garden of Music enchant visitors at Villandry. And finally, Brézé houses Europe's largest underground fortress.

programme.title: The Egyptians
programme.desc: This episode of Eternal Egypt introduces us to the Egyptians who live on the banks of the Nile, from Rosetta, where it flows into the Mediterranean, to Abu Simbel, where it leaves Egyptian territory to begin its Sudanese journey.

programme.title: The Amazing World of War Machines
programme.desc: Once man moved from hunter-gatherer to crop grower and farmer, he needed somewhere permanent to live, and to protect his property. From earliest civilization, forts, barricades and battlements were an intrinsic part of the world. Some of the oldest defensive structures still exist, and date back to the days of Assyria, Egypt and Greece.

programme.title: The Crimean War
programme.desc: The first program looks at the reasons behind the war, and why Britain allied itself against Imperial Russia.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Time slowly erases reminders of the past. Old roads are abandoned, and their destinations forgotten. When Clara's family moves to rural Hinsdale, NY, they expect peace but find eerie disturbances. Ritualistic chanting echoes from the woods, and neighbors whisper of roaming ghosts. A psychic warns that spirits are drawn to their home-and to a gruesome secret hidden in the crawlspace.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Evil thrives on deception, slowly eroding faith and family bonds. Sarah Miller senses something supernatural in her home, terrifying her children and making her question reality. Her boyfriend's skepticism deepens the divide as a demonic force tightens its grip. A religious demonologist identifies a diabolical infestation and prepares a ritual to expel the entity before it destroys them.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Some Native American myths tell of supernatural creatures guarding the dead. Early explorers spoke of werewolves and the Wendigo. When Randy discovers a Native American skeleton beneath his home, he recites an incantation, hoping to make contact. Soon, a cold, growling monster appears, attacking his loved ones. The spirits don't want the house-they want him, and they won't let go.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Some Native American myths tell of supernatural creatures guarding the dead. Early explorers spoke of werewolves and the Wendigo. When Randy discovers a Native American skeleton beneath his home, he recites an incantation, hoping to make contact. Soon, a cold, growling monster appears, attacking his loved ones. The spirits don't want the house-they want him, and they won't let go.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: How would reality change if we couldn't perceive or communicate in conventional ways? For Marie, this question is daily life. Her daughter Julie, unable to walk or talk, interacts with unseen forces. Marie wonders if they're angels-until she comes face to face with a demon. A Ouija board session turns their home into a portal for darkness, proving that evil can lurk in the most ordinary places.

programme.title: A Haunting
programme.desc: Paranormal investigators risk their own safety to protect others. Mary Vogel, a spiritual counselor, faces a force that shakes her faith. Nightmares consume her, unseen entities attack, and even church feels sinister. A voice whispers, 'Your God can't help you now.' Her mentor, John Zaffis, realizes the truth-Mary is possessed, and only an exorcism can save her soul.

programme.title: Death in the Bunker
programme.desc: Death In The Bunker: The True Story of Hitler's Downfall examines the final 10 days in the Berlin Führerbunker deep below the Chancellery of the Reich. Includes interviews with Hitler's confidants and eyewitnesses including Hitler's Secretary Traudl Junge who after typing out Hitler's will, remained in the bunker until his death. Learn firsthand what happened in the bunker right to the very end.

programme.title: Maestros of the Camps
programme.desc: From Europe to Asia and America, music has been written in secret by prisoners of all origins and religions in the concentration camps of the Second World War. Professional composers or amateur musicians, they left gems in all styles and genres: songs and masses, sonatas and tangos. Written on toilet paper, by night at candle light, sometimes destroyed, most of these works have never been heard.

programme.title: Castles & Palaces of Europe
programme.desc: From the 16th to the 18th centuries, the Dukes of Savoy surrounded Turin with a 'crown' of residencies. The Palazzo Reale, today houses ceremonial swords and weapons, while the shroud of Turin is kept in the adjoining cathedral of Saint John the Baptist. The Reggia di Venaria, which was formerly a barracks during Bonaparte's conquest of Italy, has been renovated, narrowly escaping ruin.

programme.title: Nazi Creatures
programme.desc: Hitler, Goring, Himmler: the three architects of the Final Solution. They, like many other high ranking Nazis, shared a fascination with the animal world. In the last days of the Nazi regime, Hitler risked his life every day, leaving the safety of the bunker to walk his beloved dog, Blondi. But the Nazis' interest went beyond love of their pets or the animal welfare laws they introduced.

programme.title: The Last Journey of the Vikings
programme.desc: In the second half of the 900s, the Vikings return to France, but this time they choose unification over robbery. With a political connection, this paves the way for the Duchy of Normandy.

programme.title: King Arthur: The Legend
programme.desc: Rich with dramatic reconstructions and lavish photography of ancient heritage sites and mystic Celtic landscapes, this thrilling programme, reveals how the stories of King Arthur have grown and developed across a thousand years. The Legend is alive and well today, on screen and in print, intriguing a new generation who are in search of an inspiring hero-figure and a Camelot for their own age.

programme.title: Caligula's Hidden Legacy
programme.desc: At the heart of a volcanic lake near Rome lay one of antiquity's greatest mysteries: Caligula's vast pleasure ships. Known as the Ships of Nemi, these floating palaces vanished for centuries before a dramatic 20th-century excavation under Benito Mussolini brought them to light. Their opulence and scale reveal the spectacle and symbolism behind an emperor's quest for divine power.

programme.title: Mysterious Hanging Coffins of China
programme.desc: Since 1999, China's leading explorer, How Man Wong, and his organization, CERS (The China Exploration and Research Society) have been trying to save the last vestiges of a lost tribe of China. They were a civilisation who buried their dead in wooden coffins hanging precariously off the side of cliffs in the Yunnan and Sichuan Provinces.

programme.title: The Egyptians
programme.desc: An overview of the largest stone giants, unveiling their construction secrets and origins.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths: The Iliad
programme.desc: Odysseus and Ajax try to convince Achilles to return to combat, but the Greek warrior rejects their appeals. On the battlefield, Agamemnon, Diomedes and even Odysseus are injured one after the other.

programme.title: Mysteries of the Sphinx
programme.desc: Across the silvery Nile from Cairo in Egypt, in the shadow of the great pyramids, is one of the true wonders of the world. For nearly five thousand years its existence has been shrouded in mystery, controversy and uncertainty. How long has it been there? Who built it and when? Why was it built? Whose face is on it? Are there secret chambers underneath?

programme.title: Elizabeth I: End of the Tudor Dynasty
programme.desc: With the end of Edward VI, Elizabeth I's struggles as Queen. Many questions arise as we dive deep into various aspects of her reign. Was it actually a misuse of mercury that spelled Edward's death? Was the Virgin Queen really a virgin? What was the cause of Mary Tudor's phantom pregnancies? Queen Elizabeth I put up a strong appearance that shadowed her deepest insecurities.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths: The Odyssey
programme.desc: 10 years earlier, as the Greek warriors had just razed Troy. Devastated by this 'war for nothing' which has caused so many deaths, Odysseus is indignant against the gods, guilty of having let this carnage happen. He wishes for nothing more than to return to his kingdom, the island of Ithaca.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths
programme.desc: On certain evenings, the constellation of Lyra is visible in the skies. Following Orpheus' death, Zeus placed the constellation in the sky, as a tribute to the greatest poet and musician in Greek mythology. Watched over by the muses from birth, Orpheus' talent enchanted nature, both trees and animals alike. A brave young man, Orpheus left on board the Argo, to conquer the Golden Fleece.

programme.title: The Egyptians
programme.desc: Zahi Hawass is still searching for the tomb of Imhotep, the vizier and architect of pharaoh Djoser's Step Pyramid. The archaeologist is now excavating an enclosure called Gisr El-Mudir, at the foot of the Step Pyramid. His teams will discover sarcophagi containing mysterious mummies - including one adorned with gold - as well as rich painted tombs. Will these treasures lead them to Imhotep?

programme.title: Lost Army of King Cambyses
programme.desc: While escaping the Egyptians 2,500 years ago, the Persian King Cambyses led his army into the desert and disappeared forever. Despite efforts in the 1930s to discover what happened to him, no clues were found until 1996 when a geologist stumbled on evidence by accident. The Egyptian authorities have suppressed news of these findings until now.

programme.title: When the Egyptians Sailed on the Red Sea
programme.desc: This multi-awards film is the tale of an extraordinary human and scientific adventure. An adventure in which we are plunged into the technical and psychological world of the Egyptians 3,500 years ago.

programme.title: Great Greek Myths: The Iliad
programme.desc: The Trojans are surprised to discover that the Greeks have suddenly left the shores of Troy, leaving only a wooden horse. Inside the horse, Greek warriors remain silent and still.

programme.title: Megapolis: The Ancient World Revealed
programme.desc: Megapolis resurrects ancient cities with stunning 3D models. In the Athens episode, witness its transformation from a small hamlet to a pinnacle of Greek civilization under Pericles. Explore iconic structures like the Parthenon and the Propylaea, reflecting the brilliance of ancient Greek democracy and innovation.
